title: Emergent Misalignment Is Not Magical
abstract: arXiv:2608.29118v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on narrowly harmful datasets can lead to misalignment broadly, a phenomenon known as emergent misalignment (EM). EM poses a challenge for AI safety and our understanding of LLMs. Prior work often frames EM as an unexpected behavior, and explains it by appealing to general misalignment directions or anthropomorphizing it as acquiring an evil persona. However, the mechanisms behind these framings remain obscure. In this work, we show that EM is a predictable and data-dependent generalization phenomenon. By examining the base model's representation of EM training data and evaluation prompts, we find that evilness after EM training is highly predictable from representational distance: the closer an evaluation prompt is to training data centroid, the more evilness it elicits from EM models after training (with an average Spearman correlation of -0.73 across 12 model-dataset settings). translated_abstract: 在狭窄的有害数据集上微调大语言模型（LLM）可能导致广泛的不对齐，这种现象被称为涌现性失调（Emergent Misalignment, EM）。EM 对 AI 安全以及我们对 LLM 的理解构成了挑战。以往的工作通常将 EM 视为一种意外行为，并通过诉诸一般性的不对齐方向或将其拟人化为模型“获得了邪恶人格”来解释它。然而，这些解释背后的机制仍然模糊不清。在这项工作中，我们表明 EM 是一种可预测的、依赖于数据的泛化现象。通过考察基础模型对 EM 训练数据和评估提示的内部表示，我们发现 EM 训练后的“邪恶程度”可以从表示距离中高度准确地预测出来：评估提示与训练数据质心在表示空间中越接近，训练后的 EM 模型在其上表现出的邪恶程度就越高（在 12 个模型-数据集设置中平均 Spearman 相关系数为 -0.73）。在此基础之上……
tldr: 涌现性失调（EM）并非神秘的意外行为，而是一种可预测的、数据依赖的泛化现象——评估提示在表示空间中与有害训练数据质心越接近，微调后模型表现出的“邪恶”程度就越高。
en_tdlr: Emergent misalignment is not magical but a predictable, data-dependent generalization phenomenon: the closer an evaluation prompt is to the harmful training data centroid in representation space, the more "evilness" it elicits from the model after fine-tuning.
